cues.text: Alright, let’s take a little pause together.
Okay?
Wherever you are, whatever your day has looked like so far,
you can leave it at the door for a few minutes.
“Leave it at the door” is a metaphor that means giving yourself
permission to put everything else aside for a few minutes and focus
on being here.
Get comfortable.
Let yourself settle into the space you’re in.
You might close your eyes, if you want.
There is nowhere you need to be right now.
Nothing you need to do.
Nothing you need to get right.
Just a few moments to slow down and breathe.
Take a gentle breath in…
And let it go.
Feel yourself settling a little more with each exhale.
One more slow breath in…
And out.
I want you to notice something.
Notice your mind, right now, exactly as it is.
Not trying to change it, just noticing it.
Maybe your mind is still a little busy.
Maybe you replay in a conversation from earlier.
Maybe going over something that hasn't ever, hasn't even happened yet.
Maybe just circling the same thought, again and again, without really going anywhere new.
That is called overthinking.
To overthink means your mind keeps returning to the same worry, turning it over and over,
like a stone in your pocket you keep touching without meaning to,
without it actually getting smoother or smaller.
Notice, gently, if there is a stone like that in your own mind right now.
No need to push it away.
Just notice it's there.
Inhale slowly.
Here's something true about overthinking.
It almost always lives in two places: the past or the future.
It replaced what already happened, wondering if it could have gone differently.
Or it imagines what hasn't happened yet, imagining every way it might go wrong.
Notice, if you can, which one your mind tends to visit more: the past or the future.
Exhale slowly.
Now, I want to bring you somewhere else entirely.
Right here.
Feel your body, exactly where it is, right now.
Not where it was an hour ago.
Not where it will be later today.
Just here, in this exact chair, or this exact bed, this exact floor.
This is what it means to be present.
Being present simply means paying attention to what’s happening right now.
Not thinking about what happened before.
Not worrying about what might happen later.
Just being here, in this moment, and noticing what you can see, hear, feel,
and experience right now.
Okay?
Inhale, and as you do, notice this breath.
Not yesterday's breath.
Not tomorrow's.
This one, right now, entering your body.
Exhale, and notice it leaving.
Breath is strange.
You can't breathe yesterday's air.
You can't breathe tomorrow's either.
Every single breath only ever happens in the present moment.
Inhale again, slowly.
If your mind wanders, by wanders I mean if you start thinking about other things,
that's completely fine.
That's not failure.
That's just what minds do.
Gently, without frustration, just notice it happened, and then come back here,
to this breath, to this moment.
Exhale slowly.
Try this now.
Bring to mind that same worried thought from earlier, that same small stone you noticed.
Let yourself touch it once, just briefly.
And now, gently, put it back down.
Not by force.
Not by pushing it away hard.
Just by turning your attention back here, to your breath, to your body,
to this present moment.
Inhale.
And notice, right now, the physical feeling of sitting or lying down.
The weight of your body.
The temperature of the air around you.
These things are only happening now.
They're not thoughts about the past or future.
They're simply what's real, right in this moment.
And exhale completely.
Overthinking will probably visit again later today.
That's alright.
It's just something minds do sometimes.
But you know a way back.
Right here, to your breath, to your body, to this present moment, whenever you need it.
And if you’d like, you can repeat a few phrases after me.
I don't have to solve every thought that visits me.
I don't have to solve every thought that visits me.
I can gently return here, to this breath, whenever I need to.
I can gently return here, to this breath, whenever I need to.
The present moment is always available to me.
The present moment is always available to me.
I am not my thoughts.
I am the one noticing them.
I am not my thoughts.
I am the one noticing them.
Right now I am safe.
Right now I am safe.
Take one more slow inhale.
And exhale, completely.
When you're ready to come back, start noticing small things around you.
Whatever is supporting your body right now.
Sounds nearby.
Your breath.
Move your fingers gently.
Then move your feet.
Whenever it feels right, let your eyes open.
